extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and evaluative standards governing amendments, affidavits, and other replies filed after final rejection, after allowance, or in related reexamination proceedings, including timing, entry standards, examiner actions, fees, and expedited processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental action when amendment delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental action should be prepared when an amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the Technology Center later; it need not reiterate all portions of the previous action but should specify which portions are to be disregarded and point out that the period for reply runs from the mailing of the supplemental action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action should be headed “Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).”

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent ink requirement for filed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' to be used on papers which will become part of the record; so-called 'Easily Erasable' paper may not provide a 'permanent' copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because papers are maintained in an Image File Wrapper, the type of paper is unlikely to be an issue so long as the Office is able to scan and reproduce the papers that were filed. See MPEP § 608.01 for more discussion on acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees when adding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must pay excess claims fees for each claim that is in excess of 3 in independent form or in excess of 20 total claims; fees for a proper multiple dependent claim are calculated based on the number of claims to which it refers and a separate fee is required in each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding new claims that increase the number beyond previously paid-for claims (after accounting for canceled claims), the required excess claims fees must be paid before the examiner considers the new claim. Nonelected claims withdrawn from consideration after a restriction requirement are included in fee determination unless canceled. See MPEP § 607 and 37 CFR 1.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of amendments permitted after final action (37 CFR 1.116(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final rejection or other final action (but before or on the same date of filing an appeal): (1) amendments canceling claims or complying with form requirements set forth in a previous Office action; (2) amendments presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; (3) amendments touching the merits may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission is subject to the rules in 37 CFR 1.116; see also restrictions in reexamination proceedings per § 1.981 and 41.77(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission/refusal of after-final amendments does not affect appeal/abandonment status
rubrics_metrics.description: The admission of, or refusal to admit, any amendment after a final rejection, final action, or action closing prosecution will not relieve the application or reexamination from being subject to appeal or from possible abandonment/termination or limitation of further prosecution under applicable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See references to appeal and reexamination termination rules (e.g., §§ 1.135, 1.550(d), 1.957(b)/(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/other evidence after final require good and sufficient reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or other evidence submitted after a final rejection or other final action (but before or on the same date of filing an appeal) may be admitted upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why it is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No affidavit or other evidence may be made in an inter partes reexamination after the right of appeal notice under § 1.953 except as provided in § 1.981 or permitted by § 41.77(b)(1). See 37 CFR 1.116(e)-(f) and MPEP § 1206 for after-final affidavit/declaration practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-appeal amendment/evidence limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision on appeal, amendments, affidavits, and other evidence can only be made as provided in §§ 1.198 and 1.981, or to carry into effect a recommendation under § 41.50(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-appeal additions are tightly constrained; consult cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior art exception/disqualification submissions after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant submissions concerning the prior art exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) or prior art disqualification under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) are entitled to consideration even after a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a final rejection is obviated by a timely reply showing entitlement, the Office should acknowledge by modifying claim status or reopening prosecution if necessary. Failure to properly submit such entitlement following the first Office action may be considered failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution. See 37 CFR 1.704(c) and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview after final—limited allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: One personal interview by applicant may be entertained after final action if circumstances warrant; generally only one request for a personal interview after final should be granted, though in exceptional circumstances the examiner may initiate a second interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion applies; such interviews are exceptional and intended only if they would materially assist in placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to file multiple claim breadths early
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to include, at filing or no later than the first reply, claims varying from the broadest to which they believe they are entitled to the most detailed claims they are willing to accept to alleviate prosecution difficulties after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a claim set with varying breadths reduces need for after-final amendments and simplifies prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period / timing rules for replies to final rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant initially replies within 2 months to a final rejection that sets a 3‑month shortened statutory period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the 3‑month period, the period for reply for extension‑fee calculation is the date the advisory action is mailed, but in no event beyond 6 months from the final rejection. Final rejections must include specified form language notifying of the shortened statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure applies only to a first reply to a final rejection. Failure to file a reply during the shortened period results in abandonment. The exact mandatory wording to appear in final rejections is provided in the MPEP (form paragraphs referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments after final is not a matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot, as a matter of right, amend finally rejected claims, add new claims after final rejection, or reinstate previously canceled claims; except where amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, or removes issues for appeal, compliance with the showing required by 37 CFR 1.116(b)(3) is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/evidence after final are entered only upon good and sufficient reasons in compliance with 37 CFR 1.116(e). Failure to properly reply under 37 CFR 1.113 results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible replies under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final rejection is limited to: (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116; (B) a Notice of Appeal (and appeal fee); or (C) a request for continued examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission meeting 1.111 and the RCE fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 37 CFR 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant patent applications filed before June 8, 1995, and design applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when final rejection found premature
rubrics_metrics.description: If on reconsideration the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, the examiner should withdraw the finality of the rejection while the application is still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 706.07(d)–(f) for withdrawal of finality procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when proposed amendment not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposed amendment does not place the case in better form for appeal nor in condition for allowance, applicant should be promptly informed (whenever possible within the statutory period); refusal to enter should not be arbitrary and should give sufficient consideration. Specific deficiencies need not always be discussed, but new matter must be identified and reasons concisely expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative reasons for nonentry include: (A) amended claims would not avoid rejections; (B) amendment raises new matter; (C) amendment presents new issues requiring further consideration or search; (D) addition of claims without canceling finally rejected claims does not place case in better condition for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should indicate status of each claim and use of advisory action forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed in the amendment and which proposed claims would be entered on filing of an appeal; when entered for appeal the examiner must indicate which rejections would be used to reject the new/ amended claims. Use form PTOL‑303 (Advisory Action) and form paragraph 7.169 as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information assists the applicant in filing a brief consistent with amended claims and clarifies appeal issues. Form paragraph 7.169 details how to state proposed rejections for appeal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing expectations for examiner response to after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within an average of 11 calendar days from receipt by the examiner; a reply to an amendment after final should be mailed within 30 days of receipt by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If delays are expected in mailing a Notice of Allowability, examiner should notify applicant (e.g., via interview) to avoid unnecessary appeal or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-delivery and where to file hand-carried papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-carried papers for Technology Centers may only be delivered to the Customer Service Window; effective Dec 1, 2003, all official patent application correspondence that is hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Service Window with limited exceptions; hand-carried amendments and other replies after final rejection will no longer be accepted in the TCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Envelopes should be correctly addressed; patent application read-only optical discs and other non-paper hand-carried submissions must also be delivered to the Customer Service Window. See MPEP §§ 501–502 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited procedure for processing after-final amendments/replies (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedited processing procedure exists: e-filed amendments/replies should be described as 'amendment after final rejection' to assign a document code; paper replies must be marked 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert TC Number)' and the envelope 'Mail Stop AF' to receive expedited handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt, Mail Center will specially process and upload scanned image into the file wrapper; the SPE ensures prompt examiner action; USPTO goal is to mail the examiner's action within 1 month from receipt. If no action is received within expected time plus mailing time, contact the SPE or TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle practice after allowance (prosecution closed)
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims in an application have been allowed the prosecution on the merits is closed (Ex parte Quayle). Amendments touching the merits are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection though prosecution may be continued as to formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 (Quayle Action) to notify applicant of remaining formal matters and set a shortened two‑month statutory period (extendable up to six months total statutory maximum). See MPEP § 714.20 for amendments entered in part and § 607 for fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments received after mailing notice of allowance (status under 37 CFR 1.312)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment that does not reach the Office until after the notice of allowance has been mailed has the status of one filed under 37 CFR 1.312; its entry is a matter of grace. If filed before mailing but received by the examiner after mailing, entry may still be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved, examiner may enter the amendment and provide a supplemental notice of allowance or withdraw the application from issue; the application will not be withdrawn from issue for entry of an amendment that would reopen prosecution if the prior Office action closed the application to further amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and requirements for amendments after allowance (37 CFR 1.312)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after allowance include changes to specification, drawings, claims, inventorship, submission of prior art, correction of inventor name spelling/order, etc., and must comply with 37 CFR 1.312 and other applicable requirements (e.g., 1.121, 1.97, 1.98). An amendment under 1.312 must be filed on or before payment of the issue fee (except where required by Office of Data Management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiners may enter amendments correcting merely formal matters without forwarding for supervisory approval; amendments affecting disclosure or claim scope or adding claims require supervisory approval. Entry may be recommended if amendment (A) is needed for proper disclosure or protection and (B) requires no substantial additional work by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statements accompanying amendments after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: For amendments affecting disclosure, scope of any claim, or adding a claim under 37 CFR 1.312, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(c) with respect to pointing out patentable novelty apply; see MPEP §§ 713.04 and 713.10 for interview guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after allowance not to be used for continued prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 is not to be used as a vehicle for continued prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution should be complete including editorial revision at the time of the Notice of Allowance; amendments after allowance are limited to the purposes and conditions set forth in 37 CFR 1.312 and MPEP guidance.
